meta.name: Belize Directory Design System
meta.description: Comprehensive design system for the Belize local business directory application

core.name: KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid)
core.description: Prioritize straightforward solutions over clever or complex ones. Avoid over-engineering.
core.application: Choose readability over cleverness in all implementations

core.name: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
core.description: Don't implement features unless needed NOW. Avoid speculative architecture.
core.application: Build for current requirements, not hypothetical future ones

core.name: Component-First
core.description: Components should be reusable, composable, and self-contained.
core.application: Co-locate styles, tests, and logic with components. Follow vertical slice architecture.

core.name: Token-Only Rule
core.description: ALWAYS use design system tokens for colors, typography, spacing, border radius, and shadows.
core.application: NEVER use hard-coded style values. Update design tokens if needed, never inline styles.

philosophy.composition: Prefer composition over inheritance. Build complex UIs from simple, reusable primitives.
philosophy.performance: Focus on clean, readable code. Let React 19's compiler handle optimizations. Only memoize when profiling reveals actual issues.
philosophy.accessibility: All components must be keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly. Use semantic HTML.
philosophy.responsiveness: Mobile-first approach. All layouts must work from 320px to 4K displays.
philosophy.themeable: All components must support both light and dark themes via CSS variables.

colorSystem.approach: Semantic color tokens using HSL values via CSS variables
colorSystem.implementation: All colors are theme-aware and defined in src/index.css
colorSystem.usage: Use Tailwind classes like 'bg-primary', 'text-foreground', never hard-coded colors

primary.purpose: Main brand color for primary actions and emphasis

secondary.purpose: Secondary brand color for supporting actions

accent.purpose: Accent color for highlights and attention-grabbing elements

input.purpose: Input field borders in default state

chart.description: Color palette for charts and data visualization

sans.usage: Body text, UI elements, most content

h3.usage: Card titles, component headers, sidebar sections

body.usage: Body text, buttons, form labels, primary content

small.usage: Secondary text, captions, helper text, badges

guidelines: Use sans-serif (Anek Latin) for all UI elements and body text
Use serif (Andada Pro) sparingly for decorative headings when needed
Never hard-code font sizes - always use text-h1, text-h2, text-h3, text-body, or text-small
Maintain minimum 1.375 line-height ratio for body text for readability
Use font-semibold (600) for headings, font-medium (500) for emphasis, font-normal (400) for body
Use spacing-4 (16px) as default component padding
Use spacing-6 (24px) for section gaps within cards
Use spacing-2 (8px) or spacing-3 (12px) for tight element spacing
Always use tokens (p-4, gap-6, space-y-2) never hard-coded pixel values
Maintain consistent vertical rhythm using the 8pt grid

usage.lg: Default radius for cards, inputs, buttons, most UI elements

guidelines: Use rounded-lg as default for all rectangular elements (cards, inputs, buttons)
Use rounded-full for circular elements (avatars, icon-only buttons)
Maintain consistency - don't mix different radius values without reason
Child elements should use slightly smaller radius if nested

usage.sm: Cards in default state, subtle elevation
usage.xl: Floating action buttons, important elevated UI

guidelines: Cards use shadow-sm by default
Hover states typically upgrade from shadow-sm to shadow-md
Modals and popovers use shadow-lg
Keep shadows subtle - avoid heavy drop shadows
Shadows are theme-aware and adjust automatically
All color/background transitions use 200ms by default
Theme transitions use 300ms for smooth appearance
Hover states use default transition duration
Respect prefers-reduced-motion for accessibility
Use transition-colors for color-only transitions
transitions.implementation: Set globally in src/index.css, applied to all elements automatically

Button.description: Primary interactive element for actions and navigation

primary.usage: Main CTAs, primary actions, submit buttons

ghost.usage: Subtle actions, icon buttons, menu items

muted.usage: Disabled-looking but interactive buttons, low-priority actions

sm.usage: Compact UIs, inline actions, tight spaces

lg.usage: Hero CTAs, prominent actions, marketing pages

iconOnly.description: Circular button with only an icon, no text
iconOnly.usage: Icon buttons, action menus, compact controls

guidelines: Primary buttons should appear only once per section for clear hierarchy
Use outline or ghost variants for secondary actions to reduce visual weight
Icon-only buttons must have aria-label for accessibility
Button text should be concise action verbs (Submit, Delete, Edit, etc.)
Destructive actions should use destructive or danger variants to signal risk

Card.description: Container component for grouping related content with consistent styling

Card.className: rounded-lg border border-border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-sm

CardHeader.usage: Top section for titles and descriptions

CardFooter.usage: Bottom section for actions or metadata

basic.description: Simple card with title and content

withDescription.description: Card with title, subtitle, and content

withImage.description: Card with image at top (ListingCard pattern)

guidelines: Always wrap card contents in proper structure (CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter)
Use CardTitle for the main heading, CardDescription for subtitles
Images should have rounded-t-lg to match card top corners
Card padding is consistent at p-6 for all sections
Cards use shadow-sm by default, shadow-md on hover for interactive cards

Input.description: Form input field with optional icons and states
Input.baseStyle: flex h-10 w-full rounded-md border border-input bg-transparent px-3 py-2 text-body

leftIcon.usage: Icon positioned at left inside input
leftIcon.implementation: Absolute positioned icon with pl-10 on input

rightIcon.usage: Icon positioned at right inside input
rightIcon.implementation: Absolute positioned icon with pr-10 on input

states.error: Add border-destructive class for error state

guidelines: Always provide proper type attribute for correct keyboard on mobile
Use leftIcon for search or filter inputs
Use rightIcon for password visibility toggle or clear button
Pair with label element for accessibility
Use placeholder for hints, not instructions

Badge.description: Small label for status, categories, or metadata

style.base: inline-flex items-center rounded-md px-2.5 py-0.5 text-small font-semibold

guidelines: Use specific status variants (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) for listing statuses
Keep badge text short (1-2 words)
Badges are inline elements, can be placed inline with text
Use semantic variants that match the meaning (don't use 'approved' for errors)

Alert.description: Notification component for important messages and feedback
guidelines: Use AlertTitle for the main message, AlertDescription for details
Place at top of forms or sections where context is needed
Keep messages concise and actionable
Use destructive variant sparingly for true errors only
Can include icons in AlertTitle for visual emphasis

Select.description: Dropdown select input for choosing from options
Select.baseStyle: flex h-10 w-full rounded-md border border-input bg-transparent px-3 py-2 text-body
guidelines: Similar styling to Input component for consistency
Use for 5+ options (use radio buttons for fewer options)
First option can be placeholder with empty value
Always provide label for accessibility

Checkbox.description: Checkbox input for boolean selections or multi-select
guidelines: Use for single boolean choices or multi-select scenarios
Always pair with label text
Use in groups for filtering or feature selection
Ensure keyboard navigable and proper focus states

Tabs.description: Tab navigation for switching between content sections
guidelines: Use for switching between related content views
Keep tab labels short and clear
Active tab should have clear visual distinction
Content should change without page reload

Avatar.description: User profile image or fallback initials
guidelines: Use rounded-full for circular avatars
Provide fallback initials when no image available
Common sizes: size-8, size-10, size-12
Use in user profiles, comments, listings

Skeleton.description: Loading placeholder that mimics content structure
guidelines: Use during data loading states
Match skeleton shape to actual content layout
Animate with pulse effect for loading indication
Replace with actual content when loaded

structure.responsive: Slides out on mobile with toggle

navigation.grouping: Items grouped by section (Public, Owner, Admin, Design System)

guidelines: Use Sidebar for app-wide navigation
Group related pages under section headings
Active page highlighted with sidebar-primary background
Icons should be 20px (h-5 w-5) for consistency

Header.description: Top header bar with page title and actions
guidelines: Displays current page title
Includes theme toggle and user menu
Fixed height, full width
Mobile: includes sidebar toggle button

patterns.sidebar: Hidden on mobile (<lg), fixed visible on desktop (lg:)
patterns.grid: Single column on mobile, multi-column on larger screens (grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3)
patterns.spacing: Smaller padding on mobile (p-4), larger on desktop (lg:p-8)
patterns.typography: Base sizes optimized for mobile, scale up on larger screens if needed

guidelines: Test all layouts from 320px to 1920px widths
Use grid for card layouts: grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3
Stack elements vertically on mobile, horizontal on desktop
Touch targets minimum 44x44px on mobile

composition: CardHeader with title, description, optional badge
CardContent with details (address, phone, hours, tags)
ListingCard.usage: List views, search results, featured sections

FormPattern.buttons: Primary submit on right, secondary cancel on left

DashboardCard.description: Metric or status card in dashboards

FilterBar.description: Horizontal bar with filters and search
FilterBar.layout: Flex row, wraps on small screens
FilterBar.usage: Above list views for filtering content

lists.empty: Show empty state message when no items

tables.responsive: Horizontal scroll on mobile, full table on desktop
tables.actions: Right-aligned action column with icon buttons

focus.visibility: Only visible on keyboard navigation, not mouse clicks
focus.all: All interactive elements must have visible focus state

loading.preservation: Maintain layout during loading to prevent shifts
loading.feedback: Visual indication that content is loading

errors.inline: Show below field with text-destructive and icon
errors.form: Alert component at top of form with destructive variant
errors.toast: Optional toast notifications for async actions

requirements: Focus states visible for keyboard users
Semantic HTML elements (button, nav, main, section, etc.)
ARIA labels for icon-only buttons and complex components
Form labels properly associated with inputs
testing: Verify contrast ratios in both themes

theming.implementation: CSS variables with light/dark mode toggle
testing: All components work in both light and dark themes
Colors use semantic tokens, not hard-coded values
Contrast ratios maintained in both themes

components.ui: Generic reusable primitives (Button, Card, Input, etc.)

fileStructure.lib: Utility functions (cn utility for className merging)

dos: ✅ Always use design tokens for colors, spacing, typography, shadows, and border radius
✅ Use semantic HTML elements for proper structure and accessibility
✅ Keep components under 500 lines, break into smaller pieces if needed
✅ Use TypeScript with proper type definitions for all props
✅ Use Tailwind utility classes, follow existing patterns
✅ Test in both light and dark themes
✅ Ensure responsive behavior from mobile to desktop
✅ Follow composition pattern: build complex UIs from simple primitives
✅ Co-locate related components (business domain components together)
✅ Use React.forwardRef for form components that need ref access
donts: ❌ Never hard-code colors, spacing, fonts, or other style values
❌ Never use inline styles or styled-components
❌ Never use class components, only function components
❌ Don't create duplicate components, reuse existing primitives
❌ Don't break existing functionality when adding new features
❌ Don't introduce new design patterns without updating this guide
❌ Don't use hard-coded pixel values, always use spacing tokens
❌ Don't mix different styling approaches (Tailwind only)
❌ Don't skip accessibility features (focus states, labels, semantic HTML)
❌ Don't commit code that fails 'npm run lint' or 'npm run build'

beforeCoding: Read existing components in src/components to understand patterns
Check if similar component exists that can be reused or extended
Verify design tokens exist for any new styles needed
Plan component structure using existing primitives
whileCoding: Use existing UI primitives from src/components/ui
Follow existing naming conventions and file structure
Match surrounding code style and patterns
Use TypeScript for proper type safety
Add proper aria-labels and accessibility features
beforeCommitting: Run 'npm run lint' and fix all errors
Run 'npm run build' and ensure it succeeds
Test in browser in both light and dark themes
Test responsive behavior from mobile to desktop
Verify no hard-coded styles were used
Check that no existing functionality was broken
